content.jointProblem: The collaboration would test whether GenovaMed’s Snakemake short-read star-allele pipeline can be profiled and re-scheduled using cloud resource-allocation, queueing and bin-packing methods to lower compute cost from about 9 EUR to below 3 EUR per sample and batch runtime from 4–6 hours to under 90 minutes, while preserving clinical allele calls.

rationale.text: Popović’s group combines stochastic modelling, queueing theory and combinatorial optimisation for resource allocation in distributed and cloud environments, which is directly relevant to profiling and re-scheduling pipeline jobs on cloud VMs.

sources.quote: His group studies resource allocation in distributed and cloud computing environments, combining stochastic modelling, queueing theory, and combinatorial optimisation.

rationale.text: He has industry consulting experience in VM placement policy and capacity planning, useful for instance selection and cloud cost reduction.

sources.quote: advising on VM placement policy and capacity planning models

rationale.text: His trace-characterisation and benchmark-generation work supports evidence-based profiling of batch workloads before optimisation.

sources.quote: collects and characterises traces from four academic computing sites in Serbia, Croatia, Hungary, and Romania

rationale.text: He is open to joint projects with cloud/HPC infrastructure companies and offers testbed access for joint experiments.

sources.quote: joint projects with companies operating cloud or HPC infrastructure
access to the faculty OpenStack testbed for joint experiments

rationale.text: He has a GDPR-compatible anonymisation approach, which matters for using operational workload traces and retained clinical samples.

sources.quote: he has an established anonymisation protocol suitable for GDPR compliance.

constraints.text: Any cost or speed work must not alter the clinical accuracy of star-allele calls.

sources.quote: without touching the clinical accuracy of the calls

constraints.text: The existing Python/Snakemake pipeline works correctly; the project is an optimisation of it, not a correctness rewrite.

sources.quote: We wrote the pipeline ourselves in Python using Snakemake, and it works correctly

constraints.text: Bottleneck profiling must precede optimisation because alignment and star-allele calling are only suspected heavy steps.

sources.quote: we have not properly profiled which steps are the bottleneck

constraints.text: The target outcome is compute cost below 3 EUR per sample and ideally total runtime under 90 minutes.

sources.quote: getting compute cost below 3 EUR per sample and ideally cutting total run time to under 90 minutes

constraints.text: Changes must fit the ISO 15189 accredited quality system and clinical pharmacist review.

sources.quote: Our laboratory is accredited under ISO 15189 and every report is reviewed by a clinical pharmacist before it leaves the building.

constraints.text: Capacity is limited: company staff and budget are constrained, and the researcher’s OpenStack testbed is available only off-peak.

sources.quote: The two-person bioinformatics team and two senior molecular biologists can dedicate roughly two days per week each to a collaborative project
access to the in-house sequencer, a set of retained clinical samples held under ethics approval, and a small discretionary R&D budget of approximately 8,000 EUR per year
His group's OpenStack testbed (16 nodes) is available to partners during off-peak periods.

risks: Transfer gap: Popović’s scheduling and queueing results are largely validated on academic, HPC, e-government, e-commerce, Kubernetes or simulated traces, not on GenovaMed’s short-read star-allele pipeline; the first experiment must profile the actual pipeline and test whether the methods transfer.
The pipeline bottleneck is unconfirmed; alignment and star-allele calling may not dominate runtime or cost, so the 3 EUR/sample and 90-minute targets may need reframing after profiling.
Researcher availability is unknown in the Participation record, so current bandwidth for a joint project is not established.
Company R&D capacity is small, with roughly two days per week per relevant staff member and an approximately 8,000 EUR annual discretionary budget, which may limit the scope of experiments.
Optimisation may affect allele calls or require revalidation under ISO 15189 and clinical pharmacist review, constraining acceptable changes.
Cloud environment details, instance types, spot-interruption tolerance and operational traces are not specified, so scheduling models could be mis-specified for the company’s actual setup.
questions: Can you confirm your current availability and capacity to join a joint project, since the Participation record lists availability as unknown?
Will GenovaMed share anonymised pipeline execution logs (task runtimes, CPU/memory, I/O, instance types, spot interruption history) and allow profiling on representative batches?
Which cloud provider and instance families are used, and what is the tolerance for spot/preemptible interruptions?
What validation evidence will satisfy ISO 15189 and clinical pharmacist review that star-allele calls remain unchanged?
Is the retained ethics-approved sample set available for benchmark runs, and what is the permitted scope?
Can the faculty OpenStack testbed be used off-peak, and how representative is it of GenovaMed’s cloud environment?
